key_insight: Lip Forcing is a real-time lip synchronization approach that turns diffusion video generation into an autoregressive, few-step process. It distills a large bidirectional teacher into causal students so each video chunk can be generated quickly without sacrificing alignment quality.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high latency of diffusion-based lip synchronization models, which usually require full-sequence bidirectional attention and many denoising steps. These constraints make them too slow for practical real-time use.
method: Distills a 14B audio-conditioned bidirectional video diffusion teacher into smaller causal student models.
Uses an autoregressive chunk-by-chunk generation setup for video-to-video lip synchronization.
Reduces inference cost by generating each chunk in only a few denoising steps while preserving audio-visual alignment.
impact: This work makes high-quality lip synchronization more practical for interactive and latency-sensitive applications such as avatars, dubbing, live communication, and digital humans. For practitioners, it offers a path to deploy diffusion-quality results in real time.

paper_title: Lip Forcing: Few-Step Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-time Lip Synchronization
paper_authors: Paul Hyunbin Cho, Jinhyuk Jang, SeokYoung Lee, Joungbin Lee, Siyoon Jin
